speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 5,000/μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 250,000/μL; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: Sodium 140 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L, Chloride 100 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, AST 25 U/L, ALT 20 U/L, Bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 75 U/L; TSH: 2.5 mIU/L; Vitamin B12 Level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—specifically the inability to remain still, restlessness, and repetitive movements like pacing and leg crossing—are classic signs of akathisia. While I have ordered initial blood and metabolic tests to rule out other causes, this clinical picture strongly points to a medication-induced reaction. Have you recently started or increased the dosage of any psychiatric medications, such as antipsychotics or antidepressants?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medication-induced akathisia secondary to recent initiation or dose increase of antipsychotic therapy for schizophrenia.
